## The `_quarto.tests` front matter

A test document is any `.qmd` file under `tests/`.
A file or directory whose name starts with an underscore is skipped, and so are `generated/` and `.quarto/`.
Its `_quarto.tests` block describes the case, with the keys that q2 `quarto call test` reads.
Every key other than `run` names a format to render.
A document with no format key renders to every format that `quarto inspect` reports for it, under the default log rule.

```yaml
---
title: "Backup removed"
format:
  html: default
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
_quarto:
  tests:
    run:
      extension-test:
        timeout: 120
    html:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ["Always here"]
        - ["Backup"]
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        - []
        - ["Backup"]
---
```

### Keys under a format

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `noErrors` | The case fails on a log line at `ERROR`. |
| `noErrorsOrWarnings` | The case fails on a log line at `ERROR` or `WARN`. This is the default. |
| `shouldError` | The case passes when the render exits with an error code, or when the log has a line at `ERROR`. |
| `ensureFileRegexMatches` | Matches the output file against `[[patterns that must match], [patterns that must not match]]`. |
| `ensureTypstFileRegexMatches` | Matches the kept `.typ` file in the same way. Set `keep-typ: true` on the `typst` format. A `.typ` file that is already beside the document before the render fails the assertion. |
| `ensureDocxRegexMatches` | Matches `word/document.xml` of a DOCX output in the same way. q2 does not know this key. |
| `printsMessage` | Looks for a log line: `{level, regex, negate, count}`, or a list of these. With `count`, exactly that many lines must match. |
| `fileExists` | Looks for `outputPath` beside the output, and for `supportPath` in `<output name>_files`. |

: The keys that the runner executes. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

A key applies when it is present, whatever its value.
A format with more than one of `noErrors`, `noErrorsOrWarnings`, and `shouldError` fails with `policy-conflict`.
A key that q2 or quarto-cli knows and the runner does not execute gives a `skip` entry, for example `ensureHtmlElements`.
The case warnings name every assertion that did not run, and every key that q2 rejects.
Any other key fails the format with `unknown-assertion`.

A `printsMessage` entry at `WARN` needs `noErrors`, as in q2.
Without it, the default rule fails the case on the warning that the entry expects.

### Patterns

Patterns are regular expressions.
Escape a literal dot or brace, for example `"1\\.0"` or `"\\{\\{<"`.
In `ensureFileRegexMatches` and `ensureTypstFileRegexMatches`, a pattern with `^` or `$` matches one line of the file.
In `ensureDocxRegexMatches`, a pattern matches the whole `word/document.xml`, so `^` and `$` anchor the start and the end of that file.
The runner does not translate some patterns, for example `x{2}` and `a*?`, and reports them as a `skip` entry.

A pattern in the first list of `ensureDocxRegexMatches` can fail on text that the document contains, because Word can split a text across several XML elements.
A pattern in the second list is reliable.

### Log lines

The runner reads the render log line by line.
A line that starts with `(W)`, `WARNING`, or `[WARNING]` is a warning.
A line that starts with `(E)`, `ERROR`, `FATAL`, or `[ERROR]` is an error.
`quarto.log.warning` and `quarto.log.error` write the `(W)` and `(E)` markers, and Pandoc writes the bracketed ones.
q2 and quarto-cli do not see these lines as warnings or errors.

### Keys under `run`

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `skip` | Skips the document. A string is the reason. |
| `os`, `not_os` | Runs the document only on, or never on, `darwin`, `linux`, or `windows`. |
| `ci` | With `false`, skips the document on continuous integration. Other values have no effect, as in q2. |
| `requires_js` | Skips the document, because the runner does not execute JavaScript. A document with a `check` must not set it, because the document is then skipped and the check does not run. |
| `requires` | Skips the document when `Rscript` (`knitr`) or `jupyter` (`jupyter`) is not on the `PATH`. |
| `extension-test` | Holds the options of this runner. |

: The keys under `_quarto.tests.run`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | integer | `300` | Seconds for each render. It needs `timeout` or `gtimeout` on the `PATH`, and has no effect without one. |
| `name` | string | The file stem | A human name for the case. |
| `description` | string | `""` | What the case covers. |
| `warnings` | `default` or `exhaustive` | `default` | With `exhaustive`, each warning in a `noErrors` format must match a `printsMessage` entry at `WARN` that is not negated. A document with `exhaustive` and no `noErrors` format fails with `options-invalid`. |
| `check` | string | None | A shell command that runs after the assertions of each format pass. See "Check hook". |

: The options under `_quarto.tests.run.extension-test`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[14,14,20,52]"}

A value that does not validate fails the document with `options-invalid`.
Any other key under `run` is ignored, as q2 ignores it, and the case warnings name it.
`tests/_quarto.yml` can set `_quarto.tests.run.extension-test` for every document, and each document overrides it key by key.
Any other key under `_quarto.tests` in `tests/_quarto.yml` fails `render/_config` with `project-tests-keys`, because q2 reads the document alone.
If `quarto inspect` cannot read the tests project, `render/_config` is a skip with `project-inspect-failed`.

### Differences from q2

- The runner sees `(W)` and `(E)` lines as warnings and errors.
- The promoted warnings and the unexpanded shortcode check also apply under `noErrors`.
- `shouldError` also passes on a log line at `ERROR`, because quarto-cli exits 0 when the Lua code of an extension fails.
- The runner executes `ensureDocxRegexMatches`, and its second list is specific to the runner.
- A `printsMessage` pattern matches one log line.
- `printsMessage` reads `count`, and q2 ignores it and checks for at least one line.
- `warnings: exhaustive` is specific to the runner, and q2 applies `noErrors` alone.
- The runner reads the kept `.typ` file beside the input, named after it.
- A document without format keys renders here, and q2 skips it.
- q2 ignores `check`, so the check hook runs only with this runner.

## Command line

```bash
quarto pandoc lua tests/_extensions/*/extension-test/run.lua [options]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--root <dir>` | The parent of the tests directory | Repository root. |
| `--tests <dir>` | Found from the runner's location | Tests directory. |
| `--layer <name>` | All three | `conformance`, `render`, or `smoke`. Repeat it to run several. |
| `--severity <level>` | `strict` | `strict` or `lenient`. With `lenient`, a schema pattern that does not compile is reported as a warning rather than a failure. |
| `--max-generated <n>` | `200` | The most documents the smoke layer generates for one extension. |
| `--keep-generated` | Off | Leave the generated documents in `tests/generated/` to inspect them. |
| `--json <path>` | `tests/_results/results.json` | Where to write the result JSON. |
| `--tap <path>` | `-` | Where to write TAP 13. `-` means standard output. |
| `--list` | Off | Print the plan and run nothing. |
| `--quiet` | Off | Leave out the summary on standard error. |
| `--version` | | Print the framework version. |
| `--help` | | Print the usage. |

: Runner options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,28,48]"}

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Every case passed or was skipped. |
| `1` | At least one case failed. |
| `2` | The runner could not run, for example because of an unknown option or a root that is not a directory. |

: Exit codes. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

## Layers

### Conformance

The conformance layer reads each extension under `<root>/_extensions/`, and nothing else.
Copies under `docs/` or `tests/` are left out, because they exercise an extension rather than ship one.

It checks that:

- `_extension.yml` is a valid manifest, and every file it contributes exists.
- `_schema.yml` loads and has descriptors that are consistent with themselves: known types, patterns that compile, and examples, `const` values, and defaults that satisfy their own descriptors.
- Shortcode entries use only the keys the schema allows, and each attribute group is `_any`, a Pandoc element, or a class or ID token.
- `_dependencies.yml`, when it exists, is valid, and each vendored file is present, carries its licence, and matches its SHA-256 checksum.

An extension with no `_schema.yml` or no `_dependencies.yml` gets a skip for that check, not a failure.
So does a schema in the v1 vocabulary, with a message listing the keys to rename, because the runner validates v2 only.
A `$schema` the runner does not recognise is a skip too.
A schema with no `$schema` key is read as v2 and gets a warning asking you to declare it.

### Render

The render layer stages a copy of each extension into the tests project, then renders each test document to each of its formats.
When `tests/` holds no document, it renders `example.qmd` or `template.qmd` from the repository root instead.
That demo document renders under `noErrors`, because it documents the extension rather than testing it.
It also ignores `warnings: exhaustive`.

The runner does these checks in this order, and the first check that fails gives the reason of the case:

1. Quarto finishes within the timeout.
2. Quarto exits 0.
3. The log reports no shortcode, extension, or filter that was not found.
4. The log rule of the format passes: `noErrorsOrWarnings`, or `noErrors`.
   Under `warnings: exhaustive`, a `noErrors` format fails with `unexpected-warning` on the first warning that no `printsMessage` entry expects.
5. The output file exists.
6. The output holds no shortcode text outside code, which would mean a shortcode did not expand.
7. Every assertion of the format passes.
8. The `check` command passes, when the document sets one.

Under `shouldError`, the runner does only the timeout check, the `shouldError` check, and the `printsMessage` entries.
When a render exits 0 but writes no log, the case is a skip with `log-missing`, because the log rule cannot be checked.

### Check hook

The `check` option runs a shell command on the output of a render.
Use it for a test that Lua cannot do, such as a browser test of a slide deck.

The command runs once for each format, after every assertion of the format passes.
It does not run in these cases:

- The case already failed.
- The format sets `shouldError`.
- The document is a generated smoke document.
- The document is the demo `example.qmd` or `template.qmd`.

The command runs through `sh`, from the tests directory, with empty standard input.
A command that reads standard input therefore ends at once.
The check hook supports POSIX shells only.

The runner sets these variables for the command:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `EXTENSION_TEST_INPUT` | The absolute path of the test document. |
| `EXTENSION_TEST_OUTPUT` | The absolute path of the output file. |
| `EXTENSION_TEST_FORMAT` | The format name, such as `revealjs`. |
| `EXTENSION_TEST_CASE_ID` | The identifier of the case, such as `render/check-env/html`. |

: Variables of a check command. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[34,66]"}

The exit code and the output of the command decide the result:

| Result | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Exit 0, and no failing TAP line | The check passes. |
| Exit 77 | One `check` entry with status `skip`. The runner ignores the TAP lines. |
| Any other exit code | The case fails with stage `check` and reason `check-failed`. |
| A `not ok` line without `# SKIP` or `# TODO` | The case fails with stage `check` and reason `check-failed`. |
| A timeout | The case fails with stage `check` and reason `timeout`. |

: Results of a check command. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

The time limit is the `timeout` option, and it is separate from the time limit of the render.
It needs `timeout` or `gtimeout` on the `PATH`.
With a time limit, exit 124 is a timeout, also when the command itself exits 124.
Without one, no limit applies and exit 124 is an ordinary failure.

The runner reads TAP from standard output only.
Each top-level `ok` or `not ok` line gives one entry, named `check/<n>` by its position.
Plan lines, comments, indented subtest lines, and text such as `okay` are not TAP lines.
If the command writes no TAP line, one `check` entry records the exit code.

The failure message is the first failing `not ok` description.
If there is none, it is the last non-empty line of standard error.
If standard error is empty, it is `the check exited <code>`.
The output of the command lands in `tests/_results/logs/<slug>.check.log`.

A project default in `tests/_quarto.yml` runs for every format.
If a command applies to some formats only, make it read `EXTENSION_TEST_FORMAT` and exit 77 for the others.

A `check` command is repository code.
It has the same trust as the Lua code of the repository.

### Smoke

The smoke layer generates documents from each `_schema.yml`, renders them the same way, and removes them again.
For each extension, it writes one document with every option at its default, one with every option set, a minimal and a full document for each shortcode, one for each attribute group, one covering every contributed class, and one for each format section of `_schema.yml`.

Every generated value is validated against the descriptor it came from before it is written.
A descriptor that no candidate value satisfies is reported as a skip, and so is the cap set by `--max-generated`.
A smoke failure is therefore the extension's fault, not the generator's.

A generated document renders under `noErrors`.
The generator makes inputs, such as placeholder file names, that a careful extension warns about.
These warnings are recorded on the case and do not fail it.
A project default of `warnings: exhaustive` does not apply to a generated document.
A shortcode, extension, or filter that was not found still fails the case.
A pass here asserts nothing about the content of the output.

## Results

Each case has a stable identifier.
A render is `<layer>/<document path without .qmd>/<format>`, such as `render/greeting/html` or `smoke/generated/clean-options-defaults/html`.
A case reported before any render, such as `render/discover` or `conformance/schema/clean`, has no format segment.
Two runs can be compared case by case.

`results.json` holds:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The result format version, currently `1`. |
| `framework` | The framework name and version. |
| `quarto` | The Quarto version and its channel, `release` or `prerelease`. |
| `extension` | The repository root and the names of the extensions found. |
| `environment` | The severity and the tests directory. |
| `tier` | `check` when at least one check command ran, else `render`. A check that exits 77 counts as run. |
| `layer_order` | The layers in the order they ran. |
| `status` | `fail` when any case failed, `pass` when any passed, and `skip` when every case was skipped. |
| `summary` | Counts of all cases, by status. |
| `layers` | The same counts and status for each layer. |
| `cases` | One entry per case: `id`, `layer`, `status`, `target`, `diagnostics` with the logged `errors` and `warnings`, `assertions` with one entry for each check (`id`, `kind`, `expected`, `status`, `message`, `warnings`), and `failure` with its `stage`, `reason`, `message`, and log path when the case did not pass. |

: Top-level fields of `results.json`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

The render log of each case lands in `tests/_results/logs/`.
Under GitHub Actions, each failure is also written as an error annotation on the document it came from.

## Continuous integration

The reusable workflow `.github/workflows/extension-test.yml` checks out the calling repository, sets up Quarto, and runs the tests.
It needs `contents: read` and nothing else.

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quarto-channels` | string | `'["release"]'` | A JSON array of Quarto channels, each run as its own job. |
| `node-version` | string | `""` | The Node.js version to set up for a check command. Empty means no Node.js setup. |
| `playwright-browsers` | string | `""` | The Playwright browsers to install for a check command, such as `chromium`. Empty means no install. |

: Inputs of the `extension-test.yml` workflow. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[22,12,20,46]"}

If `tests/package-lock.json` exists, `npm ci` runs in `tests/` before the tests.

The companion workflow `.github/workflows/extension-test-issue.yml` opens or updates a single issue naming the failed cases.
It takes no input.
Call it as a second job of the same run, and grant `issues: write` to that job alone.

## Limitations

- The smoke layer generates no document for a project type extension.
- A format whose output file the runner cannot place is reported as a skip.
- The unexpanded shortcode check looks for an opening shortcode delimiter in the output, so a document that prints one on purpose outside code fails it.
